This visually implies that tensor cores/ALU are a level of the memory hierarchy, contradicting the caption’s statement that compute, memory, and interconnect are separate groups.

This may require offsetting the compute box, breaking the gradient arrow around it, or adding a visual bracket that separates compute from the memory ladder.

page_hint: Chapter 8, §3 Worked Example, 'The 1.08 s budget versus the 35% planning rate'
quoted_clause: 1.08 s is the *end-to-end prefill budget* inside the 1.2 s TTFT (it absorbs queueing, scheduling, tokenization and admission overhead)
observed: This conflicts with Chapters 5 and 6, where 1.08 s is the prefill component after retrieval and queueing/tokenization/admission are explicitly scoped out.
correction: Rewrite as: '1.08 s is the prefill compute budget inside the 1.2 s TTFT after the ~120 ms retrieval allocation; queueing, tokenization, admission, and first-token sampling are scoped out in the canonical budget (Ch 5/6). If a deployment includes those in the 1.08 s, the implied MFU must be recomputed after subtracting them.'
acceptance_test: A reader can state unambiguously whether 1.08 s includes queueing/tokenization/admission, and Ch 5, Ch 6, and Ch 8 agree.
verdict_evidence: ch8:181 '1.08 s is the end-to-end prefill budget ... (it absorbs queueing, scheduling, tokenization and admission overhead)'; ch5:97 scopes those out, ch4:124 zero allowance.
fix_instruction: Drop 'end-to-end' and the absorbs-parenthetical: 1.08 s is the prefill compute budget after the ~120 ms retrieval, overheads scoped out.

page_hint: Chapter 8, §8 Mini-Case, paragraph after the four prefill bottleneck candidates
quoted_clause: If the prefill kernel is running at 12% MFU, the problem is occupancy or launch — grow the batch or fuse kernels.
observed: Low MFU can also be caused by exposed communication, memory stalls, or inefficient kernels; mapping 12% MFU directly to occupancy/launch is too strong.
correction: Change to: 'If MFU is low, use the trace to distinguish occupancy/launch limits from exposed communication or memory stalls; grow batch or fuse kernels only when the trace shows occupancy/launch limits.'
acceptance_test: The text does not infer a single cause from MFU alone.
verdict_evidence: ch8:285 maps 12% MFU straight to 'occupancy or launch' but ch8:220 'below 20% suggests memory or communication bottleneck'; :281-283 list other cases.
fix_instruction: Insert the trace step: low MFU alone does not select the cause — grow batch or fuse kernels only when the trace shows occupancy/launch limits.

page_hint: Ch 8 §3, 'The 1.08 s budget versus the 35% planning rate'; compare Ch 6 §3 and Table 6-1, Ch 5 §3(b), Ch 5 economics unit note
quoted_clause: Ch 8 §3: "1.08 s is the *end-to-end prefill budget* inside the 1.2 s TTFT (it absorbs queueing, scheduling, tokenization and admission overhead), while ~19,800 tokens/s/host is the *sustained planning rate* for capacity arithmetic." | Ch 6 §3: "against the ~1.08 s prefill budget implies a required rate of ≈ 1.19 PFLOPS"
observed: The 1.08 s figure carries two incompatible meanings. Ch 5, Ch 6 and Ch 8's own Table 8-1 treat 1.08 s as the prefill compute window (9,200 tokens ÷ 1.08 s = 8,519 tokens/s is called 'the prefill-side rate' in Ch 5's economics note; Ch 6 divides 1.29 PFLOP by 1.08 s to get the required prefill rate). Ch 8's parenthetical says 1.08 s absorbs queueing, scheduling, tokenization and admission overhead, which would make the pure prefill compute window shorter and the required rate higher than 1.19 PFLOPS. The two readings give different required rates, different implied MFU (15% vs lower), and different host counts (44 vs more).
correction: Pick one meaning and state it once in Ch 4 (Table 4-2) and reference it thereafter. If 1.08 s is the prefill compute window, delete the 'absorbs queueing, scheduling, tokenization and admission overhead' clause and instead say that those overheads are what the 1.2 s TTFT budget leaves room for (0.12 s, shared with retrieval). If 1.08 s is an end-to-end leg time, relabel it and restate the required prefill rate as a lower bound.
acceptance_test: The 1.08 s figure has one definition stated in Ch 4 and referenced identically in Ch 5, Ch 6 and Ch 8; the 1.19 PFLOPS, 15% MFU and 44-host figures are all derived from that same definition.
verdict_evidence: ch4:124 'zero allowance for admission/queue and tokenization/transfer'; ch8:181 '1.08 s ... absorbs queueing, scheduling, tokenization and admission' then divides 1.288 PFLOP by 1.08 s for 15% MFU.
fix_instruction: ch08:181: drop 'absorbs queueing, scheduling, tokenization and admission'; move those to the 1.2 s residual (ch04:124); call 149 TFLOPS a lower bound.

quoted_clause: "Their labeled 70% × 95% + N−1 policy totals: case (i) 19 → 29 compute, fleet 21 → 32; case (iii) 21 → 32; case (ii) 22 → 34; KV-only 21 → 32. The ρ = 1 u-only screen reads 30 / 32 (ceil(N ÷ 0.7) for KV-only 21 and case (ii) 22)."
observed: The policy that produces these totals is never stated, so the reader cannot reproduce them; the '+ N−1' descriptor does not match either candidate formula; 'ρ = 1 u-only' is undefined jargon; and the paragraph mixes 'N → M' totals with Ch 17's '31 working / 32 total' pair without saying which of the two numbers is working and which is total. The totals are consistent with total = ⌈N/(0.7×0.95)⌉ (19→29, 21→32, 22→34) and with working = total − 1, but neither reading is stated, and the '+ N−1' wording suggests a redundancy term that would give 47, 52 and 55 rather than 29, 32 and 34.
correction: Restate the policy inline in one line, e.g. 'Policy: working hosts = ⌈N/(0.7×0.95)⌉ − 1, total = ⌈N/(0.7×0.95)⌉ (Ch 16/17); the ρ=1 utilization-only variant is ⌈N/0.7⌉.' Then give the table as working/total pairs rather than 'N → M' arrows, and delete or define '+ N−1' and 'u-only'.
acceptance_test: A reader with only Ch 8 in hand can recompute all six host-count numbers from a stated formula and can tell which numbers are working hosts and which are total hosts.
verdict_evidence: ch8:177 '70% x 95% + N-1 policy totals 19 to 29 ... 21 to 32 ... 22 to 34' but ceil(19/0.665)=29 etc. — no additive N-1; formula unstated.
fix_instruction: ch08:177: state working=ceil(N/0.665)-1, total=ceil(N/0.665) (rho=1 variant ceil(N/0.7)), give working/total pairs, drop '+N-1' and 'u-only'.

quoted_clause: "(adding the quadratic attention term raises it to ~10.6K, activation traffic lowers it — either way ≫ 295)"
observed: The full-square attention intensity at 9.2K is ~10.8K FLOP/byte, not ~10.6K. The value is not used in any downstream decision, but it is a derived number in a table footnote that a reader can check, and it disagrees with the book's own case-(ii) total (1.5099 PFLOP, Table 8-1).
acceptance_test: The Table 6-1 footnote's intensity figure equals 1.5099 PFLOP ÷ 140 GB to the displayed precision.
verdict_evidence: ch6:87 footnote '~10.6K'; canonical case (ii) 1.5099 PFLOP / 140 GB = 10,785 ~10.8K; 10.6K from rounded 1.49 PFLOP.

page_hint: Ch 8 §4, measurement habit 2; compare Ch 8 §3 'The 1.08 s budget versus the 35% planning rate'
quoted_clause: "A well-tuned transformer on H100 FP16 typically lands in the 30–40% range; below 20% suggests a memory or communication bottleneck that should be diagnosed before scaling."
observed: The 20% diagnostic threshold is stated without distinguishing the kernel's achieved MFU from a latency-budget-implied rate. The chapter's own canonical prefill point implies ~15% MFU (1.288 PFLOP ÷ 1.08 s ÷ 8 GPUs = 149 TFLOPS/GPU), which would trip the rule and be diagnosed as 'memory or communication bound' even though the chapter has just argued prefill is compute-bound. The two numbers measure different things, as §3 says, but §4's rule does not carry the distinction.
correction: Qualify the rule: 'below 20% *kernel* MFU (measured on the prefill kernel itself, not inferred from an end-to-end latency budget) suggests a memory or communication bottleneck.' Add a parenthetical noting that the canonical 1.08 s-implied 15% is a budget-implied figure, not a kernel MFU.
acceptance_test: The 20% rule names the measurement it applies to, and a reader who computes 15% from the canonical budget does not conclude the canonical prefill kernel is memory-bound.
fix_instruction: Qualify ch8:220: 'below 20% *kernel-measured* MFU', noting the canonical 15% is budget-implied (ch8:181).

quoted_clause: "**If prefill is FLOP-bound** (as it is for 70B+ models with long contexts), the primary optimization is batching"
observed: The parenthetical generalizes the regime to a model class ('70B+ models with long contexts'), which the chapter's own §5 and §8.1 explicitly refuse to do ('both are operating-point properties: decode's intensity rises with batch, and prefill's falls as context shortens'). The generalization is also not needed for the bullet's argument, which is conditional on the regime.
correction: Delete the parenthetical, or replace it with the scoped form: '(as it is at the canonical 9.2K operating point on this model geometry — an operating-point property, not a property of the model class; see §8.1).'
acceptance_test: No regime label in Ch 8 is asserted for a model class rather than for a named operating point.
verdict_evidence: ch8:242 generalizes to a class; ch8:36/230 make regimes operating-point properties; prefill intensity 2PL/2P=L so model size not the variable.
fix_instruction: Delete the '70B+ models' parenthetical or scope it to the 9.2K operating point per ch8:36.
